content:
I'm writing to ask if there exists a data structure with algorithm that implements the pseudo-code described below:

def merge (l1 l2 : List (K × V)) : Option List (K × V) :=
  match l1, l2 with
    | .nil, _ => l2
    | _, .nil => l1
    | .cons (k1, v1) l1, .cons (k2, v2) l2 =>
      if k1 < k2 then
        match merge l1 (.cons (k2, v2) l2 )with
            | some l =>.cons (k1, v1) l
            | none => none
        else if k1 = k2 then
          match v1 ⊔ v2 with
            | none => none
            | some v =>
              match merge l1 l2 with
                | some l => .cons (l1, v) l
                | none => none
        else
          match merge (.cons (k1, v1) l1) l2 with
            | some l =>.cons (k2, v2) l
            | none => none

It's similar to the List.merge but additionally joins the values that associate with the keys that are equal; and the join of two values can be none, leading to the merge of such two lists resulting in none.

It can be more general, given two collections of (k, v)s, where in each collection keys are always unique, the merge of the two collection is defined to join values associate with keys that are equal and allow the join operation to be defined on option types.

I have tried to lookin into AList, TreeMap, and HashMap.mergeWithM, but they are not exactly describing such a merge operation. I wonder if anyone knows an existing data structure in the library has such a merge operation (preferably easy to reason about)?

I'm not aware of any library function that will do exactly what you want. The closest thing I can find is docs#Array.mergeDedup in Batteries, but it works on arrays (not lists) and I think it won't handle none in the way you are asking for.

However, I'll point out that you could write your code much more compactly if you take advantage of the fact that Option belongs to the Applicative type class, so you can use the <$> and <*> operators to work on optional values so that if any operand is none, the computation will automatically return none. Using that approach, here is an implementation of your merge function. To keep things simple I've written it to work only on Nat × Nat using a made-up join operation, but of course you can make it more general using type classes.

def join (x y : Nat) :=
  if x == 0 || y == 0 then none else some (max x y)   -- just an example

infix:68 " ⊔ " => join

def merge (l1 l2 : List (Nat × Nat)) : Option (List (Nat × Nat)) :=
  match l1, l2 with
    | l1, [] => l1
    | [], l2 => l2
    | p1@(k1, v1) :: l1, p2@(k2, v2) :: l2 =>
      match compare k1 k2 with
        | .lt => (p1 :: ·) <$> merge l1 ((k2, v2) :: l2)
        | .eq => .cons <$> ((k1, ·) <$> (v1 ⊔ v2)) <*> merge l1 l2
        | .gt => (p2 :: ·) <$> merge ((k1, v1) :: l1) l2

Let's try it:

#eval merge [(2, 3), (4, 5)] [(3, 2), (4, 6), (6, 8)]  -- produces: some [(2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 6), (6, 8)]

#eval merge [(2, 3), (4, 5)] [(3, 2), (4, 0), (6, 8)] -- produces: none

If the line above with .eq is too hard to read, you can replace it with this:

        | .eq =>
            let j : Option (Nat × Nat) := (k1, ·) <$> (v1 ⊔ v2)
            .cons <$> j <*> merge l1 l2

With HashMaps you could implement this in the following way:

import Std

open Std HashMap

def merge [BEq α] [Hashable α] (m₁ m₂ : HashMap α β) (f : β → β → Option β) : Option (HashMap α β) :=
  let inter := m₁.inter m₂
  let r₁ := m₁.diff inter
  let r₂ := m₂.diff inter

  let joined := inter.filterMap (fun k _ => m₁[k]?.bind (fun v => m₂[k]?.bind (fun v' => f v v')))

  if joined.size < inter.size
  then none
  else (joined.union r₁).union r₂

def join (x y : Nat) :=
  if x == 0 || y == 0 then none else some (max x y)

#eval merge (.ofList [(2, 3), (4, 5)]) (.ofList [(3, 2), (4, 6), (6, 8)]) join

#eval merge (.ofList [(2, 3), (4, 5)]) (.ofList [(3, 2), (4, 0), (6, 8)]) join

theorem getKey_mem [BEq α] [Hashable α] [EquivBEq α] [LawfulHashable α] (m₁ : HashMap α β) (k : α) (h : k ∈ m₁) :
    m₁.getKey k h ∈ m₁ := by
  let k' := m₁.getKey k h
  have h' : k' = m₁.getKey k h := by simp[k']
  rw [← h']
  apply Std.HashMap.mem_of_getKey?_eq_some
  rw [Std.HashMap.getKey?_eq_some_iff (k := k)]
  exists h

theorem isSome_merge_iff [BEq α] [Hashable α] [EquivBEq α] [LawfulHashable α] (m₁ m₂ : HashMap α β) (f : β → β → Option β) :
    (merge m₁ m₂ f).isSome ↔ ∀ (k : α) (h₁ : k ∈ m₁) (h₂ : k ∈ m₂), (f m₁[k] m₂[k]).isSome := by
  simp only [merge, inter_eq, diff_eq, union_eq, Option.isSome_ite', Nat.not_lt]
  have : (m₁ ∩ m₂).size ≤ (filterMap (fun k x => m₁[k]?.bind fun v => m₂[k]?.bind fun v' => f v v') (m₁ ∩ m₂)).size
          ↔ (m₁ ∩ m₂).size = (filterMap (fun k x => m₁[k]?.bind fun v => m₂[k]?.bind fun v' => f v v') (m₁ ∩ m₂)).size := by
    grind
  rw [this, eq_comm, size_filterMap_eq_size_iff]
  simp only [mem_inter_iff, getKey_inter]
  constructor
  · intro h k h₁ h₂
    specialize h k (And.intro h₁ h₂)
    simp [Option.isSome_bind, Option.any_eq_true] at h
    rcases h with ⟨y₁, hy₁, y₂, hy₂, h₃⟩
    rw [getElem?_eq_some_getElem] at hy₁ hy₂
    simp at hy₁ hy₂
    · have h₄ : m₁[k] = y₁ := by
        rw [← hy₁]
        apply HashMap.getElem_congr
        rw [BEq.comm]
        apply Std.HashMap.getKey_beq
      have h₅ : m₂[k] = y₂ := by
        rw [← hy₂]
        apply HashMap.getElem_congr
        rw [BEq.comm]
        apply Std.HashMap.getKey_beq
      rwa [h₄, h₅]
    · grind
    · grind
  · intro h k h'
    simp [Option.isSome_bind, Option.any_eq_true]
    rcases h' with ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
    exists m₁[k]
    constructor
    · rw [getElem?_eq_some_getElem]
      · rw [Option.some_inj]
        apply HashMap.getElem_congr
        apply Std.HashMap.getKey_beq
      · apply getKey_mem
    · exists m₂[k]
      constructor
      · rw [getElem?_eq_some_getElem]
        · rw [Option.some_inj]
          apply HashMap.getElem_congr
          apply Std.HashMap.getKey_beq
        · rwa [Std.HashMap.mem_congr (b := k)]
          apply Std.HashMap.getKey_beq
      · apply h

theorem merge_getElem?_of_mem_left [BEq α] [Hashable α] [EquivBEq α] [LawfulHashable α] (m₁ m₂ m : HashMap α β) (f : β → β → Option β)
    (h : merge m₁ m₂ f = some m) (k : α) (h₁ : k ∈ m₁) (h₂ : ¬ k ∈ m₂) : m[k]? = m₁[k] := by
  simp [merge] at h
  rw [← h.2]
  rw [getElem?_union_of_not_mem_right]
  · rw [getElem?_union_of_not_mem_left]
    · simp [h₁, h₂]
    · intro h
      have := mem_of_mem_filterMap h
      simp at this
      grind
  · simp
    grind

theorem merge_getElem?_of_mem_right [BEq α] [Hashable α] [EquivBEq α] [LawfulHashable α] (m₁ m₂ m : HashMap α β) (f : β → β → Option β)
    (h : merge m₁ m₂ f = some m) (k : α) (h₁ : ¬ k ∈ m₁) (h₂ : k ∈ m₂) : m[k]? = m₂[k] := by
  simp [merge] at h
  rw [← h.2]
  rw [getElem?_union_of_not_mem_left]
  · simp [getElem?_diff]
    grind
  · simp
    constructor
    · intro h
      have := mem_of_mem_filterMap h
      simp at this
      grind
    · grind

theorem merge_getElem?_of_mem_both [BEq α] [Hashable α] [EquivBEq α] [LawfulHashable α] (m₁ m₂ m : HashMap α β) (f : β → β → Option β)
    (h : merge m₁ m₂ f = some m) (k : α) (h₁ : k ∈ m₁) (h₂ : k ∈ m₂) : m[k]? = f m₁[k] m₂[k] := by
  simp [merge] at h
  rw [← h.2]
  rw [getElem?_union_of_not_mem_right]
  · rw [getElem?_union_of_not_mem_right]
    · simp [getElem?_inter, h₂]
      have : m₁[k]? = some m₁[k] := by grind
      simp [this]
      have : m₁[m₁.getKey k h₁]? = some m₁[k] := by
        rw [getElem?_eq_some_getElem (by apply getKey_mem)]
        rw [Option.some_inj]
        apply HashMap.getElem_congr
        apply HashMap.getKey_beq
      simp [this]
      have : m₂[m₁.getKey k h₁]? = some m₂[k] := by
        rw [getElem?_eq_some_getElem, Option.some_inj]
        · apply HashMap.getElem_congr
          apply Std.HashMap.getKey_beq
        · rwa [Std.HashMap.mem_congr (b := k)]
          apply Std.HashMap.getKey_beq
      simp [this]
    · simp
      grind
  · simp
    grind
